CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain after fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained an injury to his left ankle yesterday while on a walk with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed on the ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing a pop but reports the ankle felt extended and stretched. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle and has been present for a couple of days. He was able to walk back to his house after the incident, though it was painful. He denies any substantial prior injuries to this ankle. He has been treating the ankle at home with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing restriction. Current pain level is 8/10 without medication, improving to approximately 7/10 with ibuprofen or acetaminophen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other acute complaints. Vitals noted to be stable with slight elevation, attributed to pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history related to ankle injuries.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He and his wife regularly take walks for exercise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable with slight elevation. Left ankle exam reveals ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with soft tissue edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular exam: Capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, motor and sensation intact bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Prescribed air cast for ankle stabilization and crutches for weight-bearing restriction. Patient to walk as tolerated once able, anticipated within several days. Continue NSAIDs to reduce pain and swelling. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if pain worsens significantly or if any concerns arise.
